data.value:
I. Acceptance of Terms
1. Agreement: By accessing, registering, and casting a vote on the BSIT 3C Voting System, the user explicitly agrees to be bound by these Terms and Conditions. 2. Modification: The Admin reserves the right to modify these T&Cs at any time. Changes will be effective immediately upon posting to the System's official portal. Continued use constitutes acceptance of the modified T&Cs.
II. Voter Eligibility and Registration
3. Eligibility: Only currently enrolled students or approved faculty members of the COI Department, as determined by the official department registrar, are eligible to be Voters. 4. Authentication: Each Voter must register using their official University Email Address and is responsible for maintaining the confidentiality of their credentials. Any unauthorized use of a Voter’s account is strictly prohibited. 5. One Voter, One Vote: Each eligible Voter is permitted to cast one (1) ballot per election. Any attempt to cast multiple ballots will result in the invalidation of all related ballots and may lead to disciplinary action.
III. Voting Procedure and Integrity
6. Voting Period: Voting is permissible only within the defined start and end times of the election period, as clearly posted on the System. 7. Finality of Vote: Once a ballot is successfully cast and confirmed by the System, it cannot be revoked, altered, or resubmitted. Votes are considered final upon confirmation. 8. System Failure: In the event of a documented System failure or security breach that threatens the integrity of the election results, the BSIT 3C Admine Election Committee reserves the right to suspend, reset, or reschedule the election, with notice provided to all Voters.
IV. Data Privacy and Security
9. Data Collection: The System collects only the minimum necessary data to verify eligibility and ensure the integrity of the election (i.e., Voter ID and confirmation of a cast vote). 10. Anonymity: The System is designed to ensure the absolute secrecy of the ballot. Individual votes are permanently decoupled from the Voter's identity immediately upon successful tallying. The identity data is used solely for verification and auditing purposes. 11. Security Audit: Voters acknowledge that the System may be subject to security monitoring and post-election audits to verify integrity and detect unauthorized access.
V. Prohibited Conduct and Remedies
12. Tampering: Any attempt to manipulate, disrupt, or bypass the System's security measures, including but not limited to, unauthorized access, denial-of-service attacks, or introducing malicious code, is strictly prohibited. 13. False Information: Submitting false or misleading information during registration or voting will lead to the invalidation of the ballot and possible disciplinary action. 14. Disciplinary Action: Violations of these T&Cs may result in immediate suspension of voting privileges, invalidation of the ballot, and referral to the appropriate departmental or university disciplinary board.
VI. Disclaimer and Limitation of Liability
15. "As Is" Basis: The System is provided on an "as is" and "as available" basis without warranties of any kind. The BSIT 3C Admin makes no warranty that the System will be error-free or constantly accessible. 16. Liability: The BSIT ‘ 3C Admin shall not be liable for any direct, indirect, incidental, or consequential damages resulting from the use or inability to use the System, including loss of data or voting opportunity.
Legitimacy and Key References
To make this template fully legitimate, you must consult the following specific areas within your university and legal jurisdiction: 1. University/Department Policy: * Refer to the BSIT 3C Admin's Constitution or By-laws: Ensure these T&Cs do not contradict any pre-existing rules regarding election procedures, eligibility, or disciplinary action. * Refer to the University's Student Handbook: Align the disciplinary clauses (Section V) with the university's official code of conduct. 2. Data Privacy Legislation : * Ensure your Data Privacy section (Section IV) complies with all local and national data privacy laws regarding the collection, storage, and processing of personal information. 3. Security Standards: * Reference the ISO/IEC 25010 characteristics that the system is designed to meet, adding credibility to your technical claims. Recommendation: Present this T&C framework to your professor and the department head for approval. If the system will be used for official, consequential elections, it must be reviewed by the university's legal counsel.
